How long have the founders known one another and how did you meet? Have any of the founders not met in person?
editEdit
We’ve known each other for 8 years. Biraj was an early user of his app JS Console while he was still in school and didn’t have a laptop, and he used it to learn JavaScript on his phone. He started emailing him bug reports, which is how we first connected. When Ajit later launched Acode, Biraj became an early user there as well and used it heavily to build and run projects entirely from his phone. In 2022, Biraj also worked with Ajit part-time as a JavaScript developer for a few months. In 2023, Biraj referred Ajit to his company (LaneSquare / Pickcel), where we worked together in person for ~1.5 years. We’re now building Shellular together.

What is your company going to make? Please describe your product and what it does or will do.
editEdit
Developers are handing off work to AI coding agents, but the moment they leave their desk, they lose visibility. Shellular gives developers a native mobile interface to run, monitor, and control AI agents on their own machines - so development doesn't stop when they do. We provide a mobile app + CLI that connects to a user’s machine and gives a native interface for multiple agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, etc.) while they run in the user’s actual development environment. Beyond agents, users get full access to their setup: terminals, files with a code editor, local web apps (via an in-app browser with DevTools) and system monitoring. The connection is established via a lightweight CLI and QR-based pairing, enabling secure remote access without setup friction. We’re building this to make agent-driven development continuous beyond the desk, so developers can monitor, iterate, and ship without being tied to their computers.

Explain your decision regarding location.
editEdit
We’re currently based in Bengaluru, where we can build efficiently with strong engineering talent and low costs. After YC, we plan to base the company in San Francisco to be closer to customers, the developer ecosystem, and leading AI companies. Our product is aimed at global developers, and being in SF will help with distribution, partnerships, and faster iteration.
Progress
How far along are you?
editEdit
We started building on April 3rd and have been working full-time since. In ~4 weeks, we’ve built and shipped iOS and Android apps (both approved & published), a CLI (published on npm), a web app, and our website/docs. We’ve also implemented native UI support for multiple agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi) and built our internal protocol (@shellular/protoco on npm).
How long have each of you been working on this? How much of that has been full-time? Please explain.
editEdit
We both started working on Shellular on April 3rd and have been working on it full-time since. Over the past ~4 weeks, we’ve shipped across mobile (iOS + Android), backend/CLI, and web, and are now actively onboarding early users in a closed beta.
What tech stack are you using, or planning to use, to build this product? Include AI models and AI coding tools you use.
editEdit
Tech stack: the app is primarily built in React and embedded inside native mobile apps via WebView. We use Java(Android) and Swift (iOS) to build native bridges for filesystem access, browser integrations, and other device capabilities exposed to the React app. Our backend is a Node.js/TypeScript relay server where the mobile app and CLI maintain WebSocket connections, allowing us to relay messages, stream terminal I/O, and support remote control between devices. AI models/tools: Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, and GitHub Copilot.

Idea
Why did you pick this idea to work on? Do you have domain expertise in this area? How do you know people need what you're making?
editEdit
This idea comes directly from our own experience. Ajit built Acode, a mobile code editor used by 3M+ developers. It showed that developers want to code on their phones, but also revealed a clear limitation: as soon as they have access to a laptop, they switch back. Full development workflows are still better on a real machine. The shift to AI coding agents changes this. Instead of writing code directly, developers now run agents on their own machines that operate on real repos, local environments, and uncommitted changes. but there's no good way to monitor, control or use these workflows when away from the desk. Shellular is a natural extension of this insight. Instead of moving development to the phone, we keep everything on the user’s machine and provide a native mobile interface to run agents, inspect outputs, test changes, and manage workflows remotely. We know people need this because early users are already using Shellular to run agents, manage VPS environments, and ship code from their phones, even in closed beta.
Who are your competitors? What do you understand about your business that they don't?
editEdit
The most common "solution" today is a DIY stack: Tailscale (networking) + tmux (session persistence) + Termius (mobile SSH). It works, but it takes hours to set up and gives you nothing but a raw terminal on your phone. That's just duct tape, not a product. Then there are two new indie projects: AgentsRoom and Control. both position themselves as "remote controls" for AI agents. you can monitor output and send messages. Control supports Claude Code and Codex, requires a Mac, and has a rough setup experience. AgentsRoom is also Mac only, and is limited. Termius (YC W17) is the closest established product, with thousands of paying users for mobile SSH. However, it remains a terminal-first experience without support for AI agents or broader development tools. None of them understand the full scope of what developers actually need away from their desk. Shellular is a complete mobile environment for AI-assisted development: native UIs for tools like Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI, and Pi; a terminal; a browser with dev tools that can hit localhost; and seamless connection to multiple machines. an end-to-end ship-from-phone workflow - not just a terminal window, not just a remote control for an agent session. Setup takes under a minute: run `npx shellular`, scan the QR code, and approve the device. Ajit spent years watching 3M+ Acode users try to do real work on mobile and hit a wall every time. we know exactly where that wall is and we built past it.
How do or will you make money? How much could you make?
editEdit
Fremium with a Pro subscription. The free tier gets you basic access; Pro unlocks unlimited machines, full agent integrations, and advanced features. Pricing: ~$5 - $10/month in India, ~$15-$20/month in the US and other Western markets. Termius - a YC company, charges $10/month for SSH alone and has thousands of paying users. we do significantly more than Termius. There are ~30M professional developers globally. at 0.1% penetration and $10/month average, that’s ~$3.6M ARR. at 1%, it's ~$36M ARR. We launched beta two days ago, already have YC founders using us, and built the entire product in 4 weeks. the market is real and the willingness to pay is proven. We're just getting started.
